stories.title: Girl group Katseye are missing two members, but their tour still dazzles
stories.summary: They may have been two members down, but the pop group Katseye received a hero's welcome as they played their first full concert in the UK. The audience erupted with screams even before the show began, as the band broadcast their music videos on the O2 Arena's big screens, and the noise barely dipped for the next three hours. It was proof that Katseye have become pop's biggest property (they're currently the most-streamed act on YouTube UK) even while singers Manon Bannerman and Sophia Laforteza are on health-related hiatus. The stage felt emptier without them, but their bandmates worked hard to fill the gaps, hyping up the crowd with a succession of bass-heavy pop anthems and jaw-dropping dance breaks. "Are you happy to see us?" asked the band's youngest member, Yoonchae Jeong, as if the answer hadn't been obvious from the moment they appeared in a storm of laser lights and launched into the Brazilian funk workout of Hootie Frutti. "I think you guys are our loudest crowd ever, literally," marvelled Megan Skiendiel. "This crowd is unbelievable," added Lara Raj. The concert was only the second date of the band's Wildworld tour - but fans already knew every twist and turn from social media. Such adulation - and scrutiny - has come quickly for Katseye. Based in Los Angeles, the multinational girl group were only formed in 2023 as part of the online reality competition show. The Debut: Dream Academy. The contest was created by Hybe, the South Korean entertainment company behind acts like BTS and Le Sserafim, and the US record label Geffen, home to Olivia Rodrigo and the Rolling Stones.

stories.title: Kenya's chai tea lovers are not happy as the nation's cows run dry
stories.summary: Kenyans love their milky tea, or chai, but some are facing the worrying possibility of doing without as the country has been hit by a milk shortage. A breakfast here is often incomplete without a cup of chai, made by boiling tea in generous amounts of milk, sometimes flavoured with ginger and spices. It is often served at meetings and during social visits, with many people taking the hot brew several times a day. But now some may have to do without as supermarket chilled sections are nearly empty. Retailers have upped the price and are limiting how much shoppers can take home. The government has put the dearth of milk in recent months down to drought, which has significantly reduced pasture and hampered production. But the recent shortages are unusual, with the country's industry regulator itself admitting to "supply constraints" and "low stock levels" across the country. Muthoni Macharia, who runs a restaurant in the capital, Nairobi, usually buys more than 70 packets of fresh milk - and is desperate and puzzled by the scarcity. "Where has the milk gone?" she asked when the BBC spoke to her as she was out searching for at least a few packets to quench her customers thirst for chai. Macharia says there have been shortages for about a week - and it was especially affecting her morning rush hour. Her regulars are not happy: some opting to take their tea black - but many will not. "If they come in groups, and there's no milk tea, you see that's a loss for me," she said.

stories.title: Watch: Heavy rain causes waterlogging in Haridwar as rivers swell
stories.summary: Heavy rain has triggered waterlogging in parts of Haridwar, Uttarakhand, while rising river levels have put the administration on alert. Authorities are monitoring vulnerable areas as rainfall continues.

stories.title: Vietnam’s globetrotting leader To Lam to visit Russia, France, US in September: Sources
stories.summary: The pace of high-profile overseas trips is exceptional even for To Lam.
article_sentences: Vietnam’s leader To Lam is planning to visit Russia, France, the United States and Canada in September, several people familiar with the plans said, as the Communist-ruled country seeks to deepen ties with major partners to combat trade uncertainty hanging over its export-reliant economy.

The pace of high-profile overseas trips is exceptional, even for President Lam, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam, who has travelled extensively and hosted several foreign leaders since taking power in 2024.

The visits inflate a packed September schedule, which includes a meeting in Hanoi this weekend with Myanmar’s President Min Aung Hlaing and follows state visits to Australia and New Zealand in August.
In October, Lam is expected to return to Europe, where he could meet EU leaders in Brussels as part of a broader trip, according to three people informed about the plans.
None of the planned state visits has been officially announced and the schedule is subject to change.
Vietnam’s Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Lam is set to begin his trip in Russia on Sept 7, meeting President Vladimir Putin, before travelling to France to meet President Emmanuel Macron, three sources said.
One official familiar with the Moscow visit said the trip aims to build political trust in areas, including energy, defence and security.

Russia remains Vietnam’s top arms supplier and is involved in nuclear power and South China Sea gas projects, including in waters also claimed by China, though Hanoi has been diversifying its military sourcing.
In France, Lam is expected to attend the International Space Summit in Paris on Sept 9 and Sept 10, two sources said.
Airbus Defence and Space signed a space cooperation declaration with Vietnam during Macron’s visit in 2025, one of several multibillion-dollar agreements, although many of them are non-binding.
French firms are also eyeing Vietnam’s railway, airport and defence projects.
